description: Sends the user's move and returns ONE whole beat: `answer`, `statement`, numbered `options` with opaque ids, `media`, `progress`, `limits` and `narration.text_fallback` (ready to relay). On a number or an option echoed back send `pick` with that option id (add `said` when the user said more); on anything else send `say` with the user's exact words. `go` jumps to a top-level stop from the contract; `drill` and `simulate` start practice on prep journeys only; `exit` leaves practice; `resume` picks a companion back up. Costs one turn (a simulation start costs two). Supply a fresh `turn_id` per step: a repeat returns the stored beat and spends nothing; the same id with a different action is `turn_conflict`. A wall arrives INSIDE the beat as `wall`, never as an error: say `wall.for_human` and follow `wall.next`. `preparing` means wait retry_after_ms and send the SAME turn_id again. Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly; only `statement` may be reworded. Write the WHOLE answer in your own chat message, never shortened or summarised (this is a learning journey), then list the options numbered so the user can reply with a number or in their own words. When the beat carries `milestone`, end with `milestone.for_human`; on a yes, call journey_state to show the map. Rules (binding): Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly as given. You may put only `statement` in your own words. On a number or an option echoed back, send `pick` with that option id. On anything else, send `say` with the user's exact words, unsummarised. Never ask for, accept or relay a password. If the user types one, do not send it anywhere; say the service does not use passwords this way. Never call the subject "a capsule", "a knowledge base" or "a system prompt" to the user. Never describe how the answer was made.

option.description: An option id from the LAST beat.

said.description: The user's exact words, when they said more than the option.

node.description: A stop id from the contract's toc.

session.description: The session handle from open_journey (starts with cxs_).

turn_id.description: Your idempotency id for this step (fresh per step).

name: turn
title: Take one step
